Paragraph states 'the lily was conceived to be Mercurius and the quintessence itself' — Jung reporting the alchemical conception, so jung-reports-parallel fits; direction and quote accurate.
The link is real but the paragraph says rosemary 'was for the alchemist a welcome analogy for the aqua permanens' — an analogy, not a synonym; the relation verb overstates the text.

Paragraph: the caelum's purpose was to create 'that truth, the celestial balsam or life principle, which is identical with the God-image' — Jung's own interpretive claim, so jung-asserts and 'symbolizes' are appropriate.

Paragraph: 'Psychologically, it was a representation of the individuation process by means of chemical substances and procedures, or what we today call active imagination' — active imagination is equated with the representation of the individuation process; verb 'symbolizes' matches 'representation of', direction correct, ellipsis not misleading.

Paragraph concludes verbatim: 'the alchemical operation seems to us the equivalent of the psychological process of active imagination' — Jung's own synthesis, jung-asserts and 'is-equivalent-of' exactly match.

The paragraph says 'Confrontation with the shadow produces at first a dead balance... the alchemists called this stage nigredo' — the producer is the confrontation with the shadow, not the shadow itself; the edge compresses the agent.
Opening sentence: 'The unio mentalis, then, in psychological as well as in alchemical language, means knowledge of oneself' — direct assertion by Jung, relation 'is' and jung-asserts correct.

Paragraph: the alchemists' view of the self 'fully accords with the Indian idea of purusha-atman', and the principle is 'similar to the atman (self)' — an explicit cross-tradition parallel, so jung-reports-parallel and is-analogue-of are correct.

Paragraph: the male spirit 'corresponds to Dorn's substantia coelestis, that is, to knowledge of the inner light—the self or imago Dei' — Jung's own psychological equation of substantia coelestis with the self; direction and jung-asserts correct.

Paragraph states 'Mercurius is not only the lapis as prima materia but the lapis as ultima materia, the goal of the opus', in Jung's commentary on Albertus (who cites Geber: 'One is the stone, one the medicine') — reports-parallel with source Albertus Magnus is defensible.

Paragraph: the water's 'maternal aspect as the matrix and "nurse of all things" makes it an unsurpassable analogy of the unconscious' — Jung's own psychological analogy for the aqua permanens; jung-asserts and is-analogue-of correct.

Paragraph: 'in order to emphasize the unity of Mercurius, Albertus makes use of the expression monocolus' — the uniped image stands for Mercurius (duplex) in Albertus and the manuscripts; reports-parallel with named source Albertus Magnus is acceptable.

Paragraph: 'The alchemical interpretation of him [Osiris] as Mercurius has its parallel in the Naassene comparison of Osiris to Hermes' — Jung reporting the alchemical/Gnostic parallel; direction and claim type correct.
Paragraph: Osiris 'is the dying and resurgent God-man and hence a parallel to Christ' — an explicit mythological parallel, is-analogue-of and jung-reports-parallel fit.

Paragraph: 'the self or imago Dei which is here united with its chthonic counterpart, the feminine spirit of the unconscious', which 'is personified in the psychological anima figure' — Jung's own interpretation of the coniunctio picture; direction and jung-asserts correct.

Paragraph: the Virgin/mother goddess 'was very distinctly prefigured in the Sophia of the Old Testament' — passive construction confirms Sophia prefigures Mary; direction correct, jung-asserts correct.

Paragraph places 'the treasure-house of the archetypes, the gazophylacium of the alchemists, and the collective unconscious of modern psychology' in apposition as the same empirical reality — the correspondence between the two is asserted by Jung.

Paragraph: 'Nothing was easier than to identify this anima mundi with the Biblical imago Dei' — Jung reporting the historical identification made by the old thinkers, so jung-reports-parallel and corresponds-to are correct.

Paragraph: 'the archetype of the Anthropos... an image that pervades the whole of alchemy down to the figure of the homunculus in Faust' — the homunculus as a late manifestation of the Anthropos image is Jung's own claim; manifests-as and jung-asserts fit.
